title: ISS Astronaut Spots Moon-like Mountains From Space - Nautilus
gist: An ISS astronaut photographed Madagascar's Saririaky massif, a large Earth outcrop of anorthosite, the rock that forms much of the moon's highlands, highlighting shared geology.

insights.claim: Anorthosite, a crystalline rock whose core mineral is the most common on the lunar surface, makes up much of the lunar highlands and is thought to have formed as magma hardened during the moon's initial cooling.
insights.speaker: David Nield
insights.so_what: Background for lunar geology and resource discussions.
insights.locator: The crystalline rock makes up much of the lunar highlands

insights.claim: Anorthosite is found on several continents on Earth but is less widespread than on the moon; the Saririaky massif in Madagascar, almost 40 square miles, is one of the larger collections.
insights.speaker: David Nield
insights.so_what: Earth analogues help study lunar formation.
insights.locator: On Earth, you can also find anorthosite
